newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon labour attacks billionaire PM Hariri.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon labour attacks billionaire PM Hariri.

text.p: The General Labour Confederation accused billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri of ignoring the poor and said his policies would destroy Lebanon.

The CGTL chief Elias Abu Rizk called on Hariri, a construction tycoon leading Lebanon's postwar revival, to start talks with the unions to find solutions for "the difficult state of affairs" before it was too late.

"We don't object about his interest in business but we want the prime minister not to think and work only as a businessman when he is in power," Abu Rizk said in remarks published by Beirut newspapers on Wednesday.
"We want him, in particular, to give attention to the mounting living conditions crisis, to the problems of poor people who don't even find bread crumbs to eat," he added.

"We wish that he realises that the policies of tyranny and hunger, and the policies of cancelling institutions, controlling sectors and bypassing the law, and the policies of conquer and divide, all these policies will lead only to destruction."
Concern about poverty, low pay, dilapidated public services and public freedoms have plagued Hariri since he took office in October 1992 to rebuild Lebanon from the 1975-90 civil war.

The CGTL and opposition groups led street protests during a general strike on November 28 over Hariri's perceived failure to improve social conditions and a decision to close scores of private radio and television stations.

The protests were snuffed out by police. Hariri, who has banned all demonstrations since assuming power, said then his new government would give priority to social issues like education, transportation, housing and employment.

Abu Rizk said Hariri was ignoring mounting budget deficits and "has forgotten that this deficit has been widely continuous for years and the debt that is resulting from his policies is just about to destroy the country."
Hariri's critics have accused him of sinking Lebanon in debt by massive borrowings on international markets to finance his ambitious reconstruction plan.
Abu Rizk dismissed official "talk" that Hariri's governments have brought about financial and monetary recovery by boosting the battered local currency.

"Workers and other poor people will not be satisfied with the talk about achieving something by improving the Lebanese pound's exchange rate as people do not eat money, they eat goods whose prices are going up continuously," Abu Rizk said.
